The May 12 morning brief opens with a decisive oil signal: Brent futures surged 3.2% to $107.58 — the first reading above $107 since the Hormuz crisis began — with WTI breaking $100 to $101.37 for the first time since Project Freedom launched. The overnight driver is the absence of any US counter-counter-offer following Trump's 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE' May 10 rejection and Energy Secretary Wright's 'next few days' military-return timeline. Markets priced 14 hours of overnight stasis as confirmation that the deal track is structurally exhausted. The Gulf drone cluster of Monday May 11 — UAE (2 intercepted), Qatar (cargo ship struck), Kuwait (hostile drones in airspace) — remains formally unacknowledged by CENTCOM, a ledger of accumulated unanswered incidents that the administration will cite to justify any resumed Project Freedom operations. Iran FM Esmaeil Baqaei described the US framework as a 'grotesque absurdity' in Tuesday morning remarks, matching the terminal register of Trump's Monday rejection without adding new diplomatic content. Senate cloture on Warsh cleared 49-44 Monday evening (Fetterman and Coons crossing); Fed board and chair confirmation votes are expected this week before Powell's May 15 term expiry. One diplomatic wildcard: multiple outlets report Trump is scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping this week — the first potential China-mediated diplomatic channel of the conflict and the only remaining mechanism Trump's own '1% chance' framing has not explicitly foreclosed. Vibe 3.

vibe.rationale: Vibe holds at 3 — matching May 11 evening and carrying the trend into the morning's primary new signal: WTI breaking $100 ($101.37) and Brent at $107.58 as of 7:57 AM ET. Neither development changes the structural vibe level, but WTI's first $100+ reading since Project Freedom launched establishes a new psychological floor for oil markets directionally consistent with the EIA $115/b Q2 peak scenario accelerating. The geopolitical stack is structurally unchanged since May 11 evening: Trump rejected the counteroffer, issued no counter-counter-offer, Wright telegraphed military return, Gulf drones multiplied. The morning adds one genuinely new variable — the Trump-Xi bilateral meeting reported for this week — that creates a small but non-trivial diplomatic wildcard. China has not formally mediated the Hormuz conflict, but Chinese economic exposure to prolonged Hormuz closure is significant and its residual influence over Iran's calculus makes a Trump-Xi bilateral the only remaining potential diplomatic off-ramp that Trump's own '1% chance' framing has not explicitly foreclosed. Three factors hold the vibe at 3 rather than 2: (1) no Project Freedom resumption has been ordered — Wright's 'few days' timeline began May 11, and no resumption announcement has been issued as of the morning brief window; (2) IRGC has not conducted a confirmed destructive cyberattack on US critical infrastructure through Day 9 post-Project Freedom launch; (3) the Trump-Xi meeting, if confirmed, is the one remaining mechanism by which a diplomatic off-ramp could emerge that Trump's own language has not explicitly closed. The morning holds at 3 while noting that the evening brief will either confirm movement toward 2 (no Trump-Xi breakthrough, no counter-counter-offer, oil sustained above $106) or surface the first positive signal in over a week (Trump-Xi contact, modified US position, or overnight CENTCOM de-escalation acknowledgment).

items.headline: Zero Counter-Counter-Offer Hours 14+; Iran FM 'Grotesque Absurdity'; Strait Standstill; Qatar Breaks From Neutral; Trump-Xi Meeting This Week Flagged as Only Remaining Off-Ramp
items.summary: The 14-hour overnight window from Trump's Monday evening 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE' rejection of Iran's counteroffer has produced no US counter-counter-offer, no modified framework, and no diplomatic communication via Pakistan or Qatar that any intermediary has publicly acknowledged transmitting to Tehran. Iran Foreign Minister Esmaeil Baqaei issued statements Tuesday morning characterizing the US framework as a 'grotesque absurdity' — language that matches Trump's terminal register without opening new diplomatic space. Shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz remains at a standstill; Qatar has moved from diplomatic neutrality to publicly accusing Iran of 'weaponising' the Strait and 'blackmailing' Gulf states — a significant posture shift from the channel the US has used as its secondary Iran intermediary. The May 11 Gulf drone cluster — UAE (2 Iranian drones intercepted), Qatar (cargo ship struck in regional waters), Kuwait (hostile drones in airspace) — has not been formally acknowledged by CENTCOM as of the morning brief window. The accumulated-incident ledger from the pause (Saturday May 9 naval exchange + Monday May 11 three-country drone cluster) represents 4 formally unanswered CENTCOM incidents that the administration will cite to justify any Project Freedom resumption. One new diplomatic variable: multiple outlets, including CBC's live story, report that progress in US-Iran talks is unlikely until Trump meets Chinese President Xi Jinping this week. China's role in the Hormuz conflict has been limited — Beijing has called for de-escalation without mediating formally — but its economic exposure to prolonged Strait closure and its residual influence over Iran's calculus makes a Trump-Xi bilateral the only remaining potential diplomatic off-ramp that Trump's '1% chance' framing has not explicitly addressed.

items.headline: Gulf Drone Cluster Day 1 Post-Monday: CENTCOM Silence Deepens Accumulated-Incident Ledger; UAE/Qatar/Kuwait Pattern Consistent With IRGC Parallel Kinetic Track; Resumption Justification Thickens
items.summary: Twenty-four hours after Monday May 11's three-country Gulf drone cluster — UAE intercepted 2 Iranian drones, Qatar condemned a cargo ship strike in regional waters, Kuwait reported hostile drones in its airspace — CENTCOM has issued no comprehensive statement on any of the three incidents. The silence maintains the technical fiction of the Project Freedom pause while simultaneously compiling an incident ledger that justifies eventual resumption. Under the Trump administration's established escalation logic, each unacknowledged CENTCOM incident that occurs during the pause is not a de-escalation signal; it is a future casus belli the president can invoke when announcing a return to Project Freedom operations. Energy Secretary Wright's 'next few days' timeline (issued Monday morning) combined with Monday's drone cluster and Tuesday morning's CENTCOM silence means the resumption-justification stack is at its deepest since the pause began on Day 3. The three-country spread of Monday's attacks — distributed across UAE, Qatar, and Kuwait simultaneously — is the most geographically diffuse single-day Iranian kinetic operation since Project Freedom launched. The pattern is consistent with Iran testing Gulf state resolve and CENTCOM's pause-maintenance threshold simultaneously: each country that experiences an attack without triggering a US response raises IRGC operational confidence that the pause can be exploited for sustained distributed pressure. Qatar's public 'weaponising the Strait' accusation — issued by the state hosting the primary US air base in the Gulf and serving as the US's secondary Iran channel — is the sharpest diplomatic break in the Qatar-Iran relationship since the conflict began.

items.headline: WTI Breaks $100 ($101.37), Brent $107.58 Pre-Market: First WTI $100+ Since Project Freedom; Supply-Crisis Pricing Regime Entered; National Gas Above $4.50; EIA $115 Trajectory Accelerates
items.summary: Oil markets opened sharply higher Tuesday May 12 with Brent crude futures for July delivery gaining 3.2% to $107.58 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate futures for June delivery rising 3.3% to $101.37 per barrel as of 7:57 AM ET — making Tuesday the first session with WTI above $100 since the Project Freedom naval operation launched on May 4. The WTI $100 threshold is psychologically and analytically significant: it marks the transition from a war-premium pricing regime (where traders assign a probability-weighted disruption cost) to a supply-crisis pricing regime (where the disruption is treated as structural rather than near-term reversible). The overnight driver is the 14-hour absence of any US counter-counter-offer following Trump's 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE' rejection, which markets are interpreting as confirmation that the deal track is exhausted. Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser has confirmed the market is losing approximately 100 million barrels per week of supply from the Hormuz closure, describing 'prolonged disruptions' that could push any market normalization to next year — a supply-side characterization that supports the EIA's Q2 2026 Brent peak scenario of $115/b as the operative directional frame rather than a tail scenario. National average gasoline prices remain above $4.50/gallon (AAA); the Tuesday Brent open above $107 ensures no consumer pump-price relief for at least 2-4 additional weeks from Tuesday's close. Brent at $107.58 is approximately 58% above the pre-war baseline of $68. The Trump-Xi meeting wildcard represents the only near-term oil-price-downside catalyst: any report of China-mediated deal progress would trigger a market repricing toward the deal-acceptance -15 to -20% scenario.

items.headline: Warsh Cloture 49-44 Confirmed Monday; Board + Chair Votes This Week; Powell Expiry May 15 (3 Days); Reconciliation Finance Text Still Unissued; WTI $100 Compounds Oil-Shock Inheritance
items.summary: Senate cloture on Kevin Warsh's Fed nominations cleared 49-44 Monday evening, with Democrats John Fetterman (PA) and Chris Coons (DE) crossing to provide the necessary votes — completing the procedural step and setting up two distinct confirmation votes required this week before Jerome Powell's May 15 term expiry. The Senate must vote separately to confirm Warsh to the Fed Board of Governors and then to designate him as Chair; both are expected before Friday. Warsh's monetary inheritance as of Tuesday morning is materially worse than at cloture: Brent is $107.58 (+3.2%), WTI is $101.37 (first $100+ reading since Project Freedom), and the deal track that might have provided oil price relief is near-terminal. His first FOMC meeting is expected June 16. Whatever posture he signals in his first public statement as Chair-designate will be parsed for his response calculus to a war-driven inflation shock that no domestic monetary tool can directly address. Reconciliation 2.0: Senate Finance, Armed Services, Health, and tax-related committees must submit measures to the Budget Committee by May 15 — 3 days from now — the same deadline as Powell's expiry. No Finance committee text has been released publicly; the tax provisions are the most politically volatile element of the bill and the most likely source of Republican defections that would extend the timeline past Trump's June 1 completion target. The $72B DHS/Judiciary measure (CBO-scored May 4) has cleared; the remaining committees are the critical path.

items.headline: CISA Day 9 Clean: No Confirmed Destructive Attack; Four-Factor IRGC Trigger Stack at Highest Level Since May 4 Launch; 48-Hour Priority Window Active
items.summary: Nine days after Project Freedom launched (May 4, 2026), the United States has not sustained a confirmed IRGC-affiliated destructive cyberattack on critical infrastructure. CISA Advisory AA26-097A (April 7) remains operative — no updated emergency directive, FBI/IC3 flash, or sector-specific OT/ICS alert has been issued as of Tuesday morning. CI Fortify remains active across energy, water, and government facility sectors; FINRA's financial-sector heightened-threat alert and NERC grid monitoring remain live. The 9-day clean streak is the clearest remaining positive signal in the current environment, but it is under more structural pressure this morning than at any prior point in the sequence. The risk calculus for IRGC cyber retaliation has reached its highest sustained level since Project Freedom launched, driven by a four-factor cluster: (1) Trump's 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE' rejection eliminates the deal-progress rationale that gave IRGC cyber planners a restraint incentive — the diplomatic incentive for cyber restraint is near-eliminated; (2) Energy Secretary Wright's 'next few days' military-return timeline signals that IRGC planners are operating in a pre-resumption environment, which historically is the highest-risk window for asymmetric cyber pre-positioning; (3) Monday's three-country Gulf drone cluster demonstrates Iran is already running parallel kinetic-escalation tracks during the nominal pause — a behavioral pattern consistent with simultaneous cyber pre-positioning; (4) WTI breaking $100 Tuesday morning signals that oil markets have shifted to supply-crisis pricing, removing the market-based restraint incentive (the higher oil goes, the less Iran has to lose economically from cyber escalation). CyberAv3ngers (IRGC CEC-affiliated) targeting PLCs across Government Services, Water and Wastewater, and Energy sectors remains the primary threat vector — the Handala-Stryker template (200,000 devices wiped, March 2026) and Chime Financial operation (April 1) established the willingness and capacity to strike. Any CISA emergency directive, FBI/IC3 flash, or private-sector OT/ICS incident report in the next 48 hours should be treated as the highest-priority signal of the day.

items.headline: Oregon Fire Season Day 5: No Red Flag; 20 Days to East Cascades Onset; Structural Risk Conditions Unchanged; Federal Capacity Gap Unaddressed Day 5
items.summary: Oregon's 2026 wildfire season entered its fifth active day (declared May 8) without a National Weather Service red flag warning on Tuesday May 12. No new fire ignitions of significance were reported in Oregon or Washington. Statewide ODF permit restrictions, Portland metro and BLM Oregon-Washington burn bans, and Washington DNR restrictions all remain active. Structural risk conditions are unchanged: Oregon's 2025-2026 winter (tied warmest since 1934, snowpack collapsed to approximately one-third of normal) ensures the June 1 above-normal east Cascades onset is 20 days out and is treated by fire management as structural certainty. National wildfire acreage through early May stands at approximately 1.85 million acres — nearly double the 10-year average for this point in the year. The federal response capacity concern raised by Oregon's congressional Democrats (May 7: Reps. Bonamici, Hoyle, Salinas, Blumenauer, Chavez-DeRoemer) — specifically DOGE-related Forest Service Region 6 fire science research position eliminations — remains unaddressed by USDA or Interior as of Tuesday morning. Each quiet operational day before June 1 is a resource pre-positioning window against a structurally deteriorating baseline.

items.headline: WPA Day 13: Wright Timeline + Trump Rejection + Gulf Drones = Near-Maximum Resumption Probability; Warsh Board/Chair Votes This Week; Powell 3 Days; Finance Text Gap Widens
items.summary: Tuesday May 12 is War Powers Act Day 13 past the April 29 statutory deadline — the deepest into unauthorized-war-operation territory the current administration has run. The constitutional accountability gap compounds as Project Freedom resumption probability reaches its highest level since the pause began on Day 3: Trump's 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE' rejection of Iran's counteroffer (May 10-11), Energy Secretary Wright's explicit 'next few days' military-return timeline (May 11 morning), Gulf drone attacks multiplying across UAE, Qatar, and Kuwait (May 11), and the absence of any US counter-counter-offer through Tuesday morning collectively constitute the most complete pre-resumption-announcement signal stack of the pause period. Should Project Freedom resume within Wright's 'next few days' window, Days 14+ of unauthorized operations would accumulate against a constitutional structure where: Senate Republicans have blocked 6 Democratic war-powers resolutions and scheduled no seventh; the administration's WPA clock-stop theory ('hostilities effectively ended' via ceasefire) is simultaneously contradicted by the president's own declaration that the ceasefire has a 1% survival chance; and no federal court has agreed to adjudicate the clock-stop dispute on an expedited basis. Triple-convergence status as of Tuesday morning: Warsh cloture cleared (49-44, May 11); board and chair confirmation votes expected this week before Powell's May 15 expiry (3 days); Reconciliation 2.0 committee deadline May 15 (3 days). Finance committee text — the most politically volatile reconciliation element — has not been released, and the 3-day deadline creates a compressed window in which either Finance meets the deadline or misses it, triggering the first significant domestic-political crack in the reconciliation timeline.

items.headline: OHA Measles Update 20 Days Overdue: Last Published OR ~20 (April 22); Wastewater Active; WA 40+ / 8 Counties; School Window ~3 Weeks; National 1,842 (May 7, 5 Days Stale)
items.summary: Oregon Health Authority has not published a measles case count since approximately April 22, 2026 (~20 confirmed cases), creating a surveillance gap of 20 days as of Tuesday May 12. The wastewater detection dashboard continues to show active measles viral concentrations in counties with no published confirmed cases — a pattern that OHA officials have consistently acknowledged reflects substantial suspected underreporting. An OHA update was forecast in previous briefs for Tuesday; if it does not materialize today, the gap will grow to 21 days — the longest measles count gap in the 2026 outbreak. Washington State holds at 40+ confirmed cases year-to-date across 8 counties, with Kittitas County in formal outbreak status. The US national total stands at 1,842 confirmed cases as of May 7 (CDC dashboard, 5 days stale as of Tuesday morning); 93% of confirmed cases are outbreak-associated; 45 jurisdictions are now affected nationally. PNW school vaccination campaign window: approximately 3 weeks remain before PNW school districts begin summer closure (mid-to-late June), narrowing the window for school-community MMR catch-up campaigns. Any OHA update today that shows a material increase from 20 would represent the most significant Oregon public health development of the current week. The structural transmission drivers — below-threshold MMR coverage in specific school communities, active wastewater detection, DOGE-constrained CDC field capacity — remain unchanged.
